column1: # clues.tsv for ft_list_last — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".

You are asked for the very last node of a chain. Each node points to the next, and one special node points nowhere. Which condition on a node's next pointer tells you that you have arrived at the end, and are you returning that node itself rather than walking one step past it?
A chain may hand you nothing at all to begin with. Before you ever follow a next pointer or read a field, what do you owe the caller when there is no first node to stand on?
When more than one node lies ahead, do not settle on the first one you see: keep advancing while there is still somewhere to go, so the node you finally report is genuinely the one with no successor.
